queries: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net AS avg_net_fee_rate, cnt AS record_count, avg_net - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Record count is the number of joined fee records in each group (COUNT(*)), including records whose rebrate is NULL, even though those are ignored in the average net rate.
Groups whose average net fee rate is NULL (all rebrates missing) are included in the side average computation as nothing (AVG ignores NULLs) and never pass the strict > comparison.
If orders.recordvault is not unique, a fee joins to multiple orders and is counted once per match; recordvault is described as a unique order reference so this is assumed not to occur.

alternatives.interpretation: Record count counts only records with a non-missing net fee rate (feerate and rebrate both present), i.e. the records actually used in the average.

assumptions.assumption: The record count is the number of fee records in the group (COUNT(*)). This includes records whose net rate is null because rebrate is missing. The average skips those nulls.
Each side's average is the unweighted mean of its group averages. Groups whose average is null are left out of it.

alternatives.interpretation: The record count includes only records with a non-null net fee rate, meaning rebrate is present.

Side averages are taken over all groups with a non-NULL group average, and each group counts equally. Groups whose net rate is entirely NULL are ignored by AVG and never pass the comparison.
